brief.headline: Stop paying 100% in advance — move to 30-day credit and free up ₹8.73 L of our cash

priceAsk.summary: Match the ₹66.48/KG we already pay Sayaji Industries for the same Dextrose
priceAsk.basis: We're paying them ₹70.80/KG while Sayaji gives us ₹66.48/KG for identical material — a 6.5% gap. The open market typically asks ₹66–73/kg for Anhydrous Dextrose IP, so our target sits right in the normal range.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 100% advance payment to standard 30-day credit after delivery
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹8.73 L of our cash that's currently stuck in advance payments

brief.financialLeverage: Sukhjit Corn Products publishes no financials, so we can't see their balance sheet or how tight their cash is. That means we build our case purely on our own numbers and on having backups ready. Our ₹1.06 Cr annual spend is real money, but without knowing their total sales we can't gauge how important we are to them. The plan: push firmly on price and payment using the fact that we have Sayaji already delivering at ₹66.48/KG and five other qualified dextrose makers we can talk to if they won't budge.

evidence.point: We pay them ₹70.80/KG while Sayaji Industries gives us ₹66.48/KG for the same Dextrose
Closing that price gap saves us ₹12.95 L every year
We pay them 100% in advance — the worst terms in our vendor base
Switching to normal 30-day credit frees up ₹8.73 L of our working cash
The open market typically asks ₹66–73/kg for Anhydrous Dextrose IP, so our ₹66.48/KG target is market-fair

alternates.name: Sayaji Industries Limited (already approved)
alternates.why: Already supplying us Dextrose at ₹66.48/KG — our benchmark and immediate fallback

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: A lead to qualify: listed Indore wet-miller making Dextrose ANHYDROUS (IV-fluid grade) — exact form match; verify IP monograph CoA before any RFQ

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: A lead to qualify: listed starch & polyol maker, established in dextrose/sorbitol — looks like a drop-in alternate to Sayaji

risks: Their financials aren't public, so we're flying blind on whether they're healthy or desperate — watch their body language and don't box them into a corner that tips a weak supplier over
We pay 100% advance today, so any pushback will be loud — frame the 30-day ask as 'industry normal' and offer to phase it in (e.g. start at 15 days, then 30) if they resist hard
If they won't move on both price and payment, prioritise payment terms — getting our ₹8.73 L cash back is the bigger, faster win
We spend ₹1.06 Cr with them but don't know if that's 5% or 50% of their revenue — if we're tiny to them, they may walk; have Sayaji and the Tirupati/Gulshan leads warmed up before this meeting
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to keep working with you, but we need two things to make the numbers work: match the ₹66.48/KG we're already paying Sayaji, and move to standard 30-day terms so we're not funding your production with advance payments.
